svg.title: Keycloak
svg.desc: Keycloak. An open-source identity provider: user sign-in, federation and single sign-on, issuing OpenID Connect and SAML tokens. Step 1, Where it sits: Apps send people to Keycloak to sign in; orders-api trusts its tokens; Google and AD supply users. Step 2, Sign-in with PKCE: shop-web redirects with a PKCE challenge; password, then OTP; the code is swapped for three tokens. Step 3, Tokens and single sign-on: orders-api checks tokens with cached keys; shop-web refreshes; back-office reuses the SSO session. Step 4, Revocation and limits: A disabled customer's refresh fails, but the access token works until exp. You run the DB and nodes.

g.text: Apps send people to Keycloak to sign in; orders-api trusts its tokens; Google and AD supply users.
shop-web redirects with a PKCE challenge; password, then OTP; the code is swapped for three tokens.
orders-api checks tokens with cached keys; shop-web refreshes; back-office reuses the SSO session.
A disabled customer's refresh fails, but the access token works until exp. You run the DB and nodes.
ONE REALM FOR ACME'S PEOPLE AND APPS
Realm acme holds the users, roles, sign-in flows, keys and three clients. shop-web and back-office send people here to sign in and
get tokens back; orders-api checks each access token's RS256 signature with the realm's public keys and never sees a password.
Customers can also use Google (identity brokering); staff accounts stay in Active Directory, read over LDAP (user federation).
shop-web runs in the browser and can't keep a secret, so it is a
public client: /auth gets S256(code_verifier), /token the verifier.
The code works once and expires in 60 s (Client login timeout).
No SSO cookie yet, so the forms run: password, then a 6-digit OTP.
A passkey would replace both. Keycloak creates the SSO session,
stores it in PostgreSQL, and sets the cookie in the browser.
orders-api checks signature, iss, aud, exp and the customer role
in realm_access.roles with cached keys: no call per request. shop-web
refreshes before 5 min pass, which also resets the 30-min idle timer.
The staff member signed in to the wiki earlier. back-office sends them
to /auth, the Cookie step finds the SSO session, and a code comes back
without a form; back-office redeems it at /token with its secret.
DISABLED, BUT THE ACCESS TOKEN LIVES ON
Support switches the customer's Enabled off. The next refresh fails
(400 invalid_grant), but orders-api accepts the access token it has
until exp, up to 5 min. Introspection would see the change at once.
PostgreSQL keeps realms, users and sessions; nodes share embedded
caches; multi-cluster needs a synchronously replicated database.
Upgrades and themes are yours; Cognito, Auth0, Entra ID are managed.
